sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the petitioners that the agriculture lands of their ownership which were allotted to their ancestors almost in the year 1968-69 by the Government for rehabilitation to survive, have been directed to be acquired under the WCL Policy for the purpose of coal mining/road widening.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The petitioners jointly and severally objected to the Revenue Authority against the proposed acquisition on the ground that without any prior notice/notification and knowledge the entire action of acquisition is taking place.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Vide order dated 07.10.2022, the private lands belonging to the petitioners have been mutated in the name of WCL in Khasra year 2022-23.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is their case that petitioners are still in possession of the remaining land but the acquired land has been mutated without following the mandatory provisions of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is argued that the entire proceedings are contrary to Section 41 of the Land Acquisition Act and land cannot be acquired for private company so far as WCL is concerned.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the present petition has been filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. From perusal of the record, it is seen that the petitioners have not challenged the initial notification which has been issued for acquisition of the land in question nor the said notification is brought on record in the writ petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The claim raised by the petitioners is after the entire acquisition proceedings are completed even the name of the WCL has been mutated in the revenue records.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Challenge is made on the ground that no notices were issued to the petitioners but the fact remains that the acquisition of the land is in the knowledge of the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The same is reflected from the fact that they themselves have stated in the petition that they are in possession of the part of the land.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: They have challenged the mutation proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, it cannot be said that the petitioners were not having any knowledge about the mutation proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The entire proceedings have been done in terms of Section 9(1) of Koyla Dharak Kshetra Adhiniyam,
1957.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The order dated 07.02.2022 clearly indicates that the amount of compensation has been ascertained by the Authorities and as far as rehabilitation is concerned, the amount has been calculated by the authorities and the persons who are displaced are required to be paid Rs.5,00,000/- each and the families which are required to be rehabilitated are required to pay Rs.5,00,000/- per family.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: At such a belated stage the petitioners have approached the Court and that too without challenging the initial notification issued for acquisition of the land.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, no relief can be extended to the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. The writ petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Dinesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: No order as to costs.

"UPON hearing the counsel the court made the following ORDER Application for impleadment is rejected.
Accordingly, the reliefs as claimed by the petitioner will have to be answered keeping in mind the said decision as well.
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the writ petition is restored to the file to be proceeded afresh without being influenced by the observations made in the impugned judgment (under appeal) or for that matter the present order remitting the writ petition for reconsideration afresh.
In other words, all questions will have to be answered on its own merits in accordance with law.
Even those intervention applications are sent back before the learned Single Judge to be heard along with the writ petition and deemed to have been filed in the writ petition proceedings without requiring the applicants to re-present the same application in those proceedings.
That application be considered by the learned Single Judge on its own merits in accordance with law including the objection regarding additional relief or amendment being barred by limitation or laches, as may be advised, which request will be considered on its own merits by the learned Single Judge.
Therefore, we hold that after extending appointments to all the eligible persons under M.P. R & R Policy, 1991 and CIL R & R Policy, 2012, the persons appointed under CIL R & R Policy, 2008 by way of mutual agreement shall be adjusted subject to maximum limit of 899 employments, which have been undertaken to be granted before the Hon'ble Supreme Court by the SECL.
This exercise be completed within one month of this order.
If less posts than number of persons appointed under mutual agreement vide CIL R & R Policy, 2008 remain available, then in that event the persons given appointment under CIL R & R Policy, 2008 by mutual agreement who are being adjusted against remaining posts subject to maximum of 899 total employments, shall be adjusted in descending order of quantum of holding of land.
41. The matter would now go back to the DRRC of the respondents to carry out such exercise, which will be undertaken within two months from the date of production of copy of this order.
The termination orders of all the persons appointed under CIL R&R Policy 2008 are set aside, with liberty to issue fresh orders as an outcome of the said exercise, that too only for persons in excess of 899 employments.
42. It is made clear that the SECL will be at liberty to terminate the unadjusted/excess appointees,
however, if the SECL wishes to save the excess employees too (in excess of 899 employments)
looking to their long continuation in service, either by creating super-numerary posts or against other vacancies or in any other manner known to law, then this order shall not come in the way.
43.
In the above terms, all these writ appeals and writ petitions are Disposed of.
